office_does: The prosecuting attorney decides which crimes are charged and who is offered diversion, negotiates pleas and sentencing recommendations, and is the county's lawyer in lawsuits and its legal adviser.
race_blurb: Open seat after Eric Richey's two terms. Defense attorney Ryan Swinburnson (no party preference), who led the primary, faces Democrat Jesse Corkern, a senior deputy prosecutor; both campaign on fixing staff turnover and case delays in the office.

candidates.summary: Defense attorney who directs Whatcom County's conflict defense office and is Blaine School Board president, running with no party preference on accountability for violent and repeat offenders and on rebuilding the office.
highlights: More than 26 years as a prosecutor, defense attorney and county civil counsel; began as a Benton County prosecutor [S1][S6]
Would hold violent offenders, repeat offenders and drug dealers accountable with consistent charging [S2][S4]
Would strengthen Recovery Court and Mental Health Court and create a Veterans Court [S4]
Wants supervisors in court, mentorship for deputies and early plea offers to cut the backlog [S4][S6]
Led the four-way primary with 38.4% as of the Thursday count [S8]

safety.basis: Leads with accountability and deterrence for violent and repeat offenders and drug dealers and support for law enforcement, while backing treatment courts that 'require accountability'.

experience.basis: Runs on 26-plus years of practice and 'experienced leadership'; holds elected office as Blaine School Board president, though not from inside the prosecutor's office.

candidates.summary: Senior deputy prosecutor and the county's civil litigator, a Democrat running for the first time on consistent charging standards, attorney specialization and ending staff turnover.
highlights: Whatcom County deputy prosecutor since 2019 in the criminal and civil divisions; earlier a Snohomish County prosecutor and private practitioner [S1][S3]
Would set consistent charging standards and specialized case divisions to speed cases to trial [S1][S5]
Would adopt zero-tolerance policies for gun violence and create a Community Court for non-violent offenders [S1][S3]
Endorsed by Whatcom County Democrats, regional labor councils and several Democratic legislators [S4]

safety.basis: Pairs zero-tolerance policies for gun violence and closer work with law enforcement with a Community Court and treatment partnerships for repeat contacts driven by addiction and mental illness.

experience.basis: First-time candidate running on 'A New Kind of Leadership' and merit over seniority, though a long-time deputy in the office.
